mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a tightening labor market that will drive wage inflation, leading to a hawkish Fed response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PCE inflation remains below 2% despite the unemployment rate signal, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into general inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the industrial production index, signals a supply shock that will drive inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM manufacturing PMI remains above 50, indicating that the supply shock is not severe enough to derail the industrial sector.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, defined as an increase of more than 50 basis points in a single month, signals an aggressive hawkish shift by the Fed that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed explicitly signals a pause in the hiking cycle, indicating that the tightening is not as aggressive as initially feared.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the housing starts index, signals a weakening in the housing sector that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB homebuilder sentiment index remains above 50, indicating that the housing sector remains resilient despite the drop in starts.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating increase in nonfarm payrolls, defined as a 3-month moving average increase of more than 200,000 jobs per month, signals a strengthening labor market that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims spike above 400,000, indicating that the labor market is weakening despite the payroll gains.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the consumer price index, defined as a year-over-year increase of more than 3%, signals a breakout of inflation that will drive the Fed to tighten policy and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-year breakeven inflation rate remains below 2%, indicating that the market expects the inflation spike to be transitory.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in real personal consumption expenditures, as measured by the year-over-year change in the real PCE index, signals a weakening in consumer demand that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Conference Board consumer confidence index remains above 100, indicating that consumer sentiment remains strong despite the drop in spending.
